children.translated_text: In the <s>paśu</s> (animal) and <s>savanīya</s> (pressing) rites, there should be <s>vikalpa</s> (option), if [the element is] modified, since neither has scriptural basis for both. (Jaim. 12.2.31)

children.text: pāśukaṃ vā tasya vaiśeṣikāmnānāt tadanarthakaṃ vikalpe syāt / Jaim_12,2.32 /
children.translated_text: Or the animal [rite rule should prevail], because of its specific mention; in the case of option, that [other rule] would be purposeless. (Jaim. 12.2.32)

children.text: paśoś ca viprakarṣas tantramadhye vidhānāt / Jaim_12,2.33 /
children.translated_text: And the animal [rite] has priority, because of the injunction within the <s>tantra</s> (unified performance). (Jaim. 12.2.33)

children.text: apūrvaṃ ca prakṛtau samānatantrā ced anityatvād anarthakaṃ hi syāt / Jaim_12,2.34 /
children.translated_text: And a new [element] in the <s>prakṛti</s> (model rite), if it belongs to the same <s>tantra</s>, would be purposeless because of non-permanence. (Jaim. 12.2.34)

children.text: adhikaś ca guṇaḥ sādhāraṇe 'virodhāt kāṃsyabhojivad amukhye 'pi / Jaim_12,2.35 /
children.translated_text: And an additional subordinate element, when shared, [is accepted] because of non-contradiction, like [the rule regarding] one who eats from a bronze vessel — even when it is not the principal [context]. (Jaim. 12.2.35)

children.text: tatpravṛttyā tu tantrasya niyamaḥ syād yathā pāśukaṃ sūktapākena / Jaim_12,2.36 /
children.translated_text: But by its operation, there would be a restriction of the <s>tantra</s> (unified performance), just as the animal [rite is restricted] by the <s>sūktapāka</s> (hymn-cooking rite). (Jaim. 12.2.36)
Or not, because of non-contradiction. (Jaim. 12.2.37)
And because it lacks the characteristic of a [separate] scriptural rule. (Jaim. 12.2.38)

children.text: viśvajiti vatsatvaṅnāmadheyād itarathā tantrabhūyastvād ahataṃ syāt / Jaim_12,3.1 /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Viśvajit</s> (all-conquering sacrifice), because the name includes 'calf-skin,' otherwise, due to the preponderance of <s>tantra</s> (unified performance), [the garment] should be unworn. (Jaim. 12.3.1)

children.text: avirodhī vā uparivāso hi vatsatvak / Jaim_12,3.2 /
children.translated_text: Or [there is] no contradiction, for the calf-skin is an upper garment. (Jaim. 12.3.2)

children.text: anunirvāpyeṣu bhūyastvena tantraniyamaḥ syāc chviṣṭhakṛddarśanāc ca / Jaim_12,3.3 /
children.translated_text: In the <s>anunirvāpya</s> (secondary offering) rites, there should be a <s>tantra</s>-restriction by preponderance, and because of the observation [in the case] of <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the 'making-good-the-offering' rite). (Jaim. 12.3.3)

children.text: āgantukatvād vā svadharmā syāc chrutiviśeṣād itarasya ca mukhyatvāt / Jaim_12,3.4 /
children.translated_text: Or, since it is incidental, it should retain its own properties, because of the specific scriptural [statement], and because the other is principal. (Jaim. 12.3.4)
And because it is in its own place. (Jaim. 12.3.5)

children.text: sviṣṭakṛcchrapaṇān neti ced vikāraḥ pavamānavat / Jaim_12,3.6 /
children.translated_text: If [one argues] that from the cooking of the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> [it follows that] it is not so — [the reply is that] it is a modification, like [the case of] the <s>Pavamāna</s> [hymns]. (Jaim. 12.3.6)

children.text: avikāro vā prakṛtivac codanāṃ prati bhāvāc ca / Jaim_12,3.7 /
children.translated_text: Or it is not a modification, since, like the <s>prakṛti</s> (model rite), it exists with reference to the injunction. (Jaim. 12.3.7)

children.text: eka karmaṇi śiṣṭatvād guṇānāṃ sarvakarma syāt / Jaim_12,3.8 /
children.translated_text: Since subordinate elements are prescribed for one rite, they should apply to all rites [of that type]. (Jaim. 12.3.8)

children.text: ekārthās tu vikalperan samuccaye hy āvṛttiḥ syāt pradhānasya / Jaim_12,3.9 /
children.translated_text: But those serving the same purpose should be treated as <s>vikalpa</s> (alternatives), for in <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) there would be repetition of the principal [rite]. (Jaim. 12.3.9)
If [one argues] that [the mantra] should be repeated because it has meaning — (Jaim. 12.3.10)

children.text: nāśrutatvād dhi vikalpavac ca darśayati kālāntare 'rthavattvaṃ syāt / Jaim_12,3.11 /
children.translated_text: No, because it is not [separately] stated in scripture; and it is shown to be like an option — the meaningfulness would apply at a different time. (Jaim. 12.3.11)

children.text: prāyaścitteṣu caikārthyān niṣpannenābhisaṃyogas tasmāt sarvasya nirghātaḥ / Jaim_12,3.12 /
children.translated_text: And in <s>prāyaścittas</s> (expiatory rites), since they serve the same purpose, there is connection with what has been completed; therefore all [faults] are removed. (Jaim. 12.3.12)
But <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) serves the purpose [of removing] faults. (Jaim. 12.3.13)

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ karmasaṃyogaḥ svadharmeṇa prayogaḥ syād dharmasya tannimittatvāt / Jaim_12,3.14 /
children.translated_text: The <s>mantras</s> are connected with the ritual act; their application should follow their own properties, since the properties are caused by those [mantras]. (Jaim. 12.3.14)

children.text: vidyāṃpratividhinād vā sarvakāraṇaṃ prayogaḥ syāt karmārthatvāt prayogasya / Jaim_12,3.15 /
children.translated_text: Or, because of the counter-injunction regarding knowledge, the application should be of all causes, since the application serves the purpose of the ritual act. (Jaim. 12.3.15)
Because of the instruction regarding the accent of ordinary speech, the prohibition [applies] as in the case of <s>aira</s> (a particular recitation), by the word 'generally.' (Jaim. 12.3.16)

children.text: mantropadeśo vā na bhāṣikasya prāyopapatter bhāṣikaśrutiḥ / Jaim_12,3.17 /
children.translated_text: Or it is an instruction regarding the <s>mantra</s>, not regarding ordinary speech, since the ordinary-speech scripture is established by common usage. (Jaim. 12.3.17)

children.text: vikāraḥ kāraṇāgrahaṇe tannyāyatvād dṛṣṭe 'py evam / Jaim_12,3.18 /
children.translated_text: When the cause is not grasped, a modification [results], since that is the rule; even when [the cause] is perceived, it is likewise. (Jaim. 12.3.18)
Or, because of its origin from that, since it has the character of authoritative teaching. (Jaim. 12.3.19)

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ karaṇārthatvān mantrāntena karmādisannipātaḥ syāt sarvasya vacanārthatvāt / Jaim_12,3.20 /
children.translated_text: Since <s>mantras</s> serve as instruments, by the end of the <s>mantra</s> there should be conjunction with the beginning of the ritual act, because the words of all [mantras] have purpose. (Jaim. 12.3.20)
Because of the word 'continuous,' the conjunction with the beginning [is maintained] during the pouring. (Jaim. 12.3.21)
Or [it is] a continuation of the ritual act, since there are multiple acts, and the other [interpretation] is impossible. (Jaim. 12.3.22)
And in the <s>āghāra</s> (preliminary libation), because of the long duration of pouring. (Jaim. 12.3.23)

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ saṃnipātitvād ekārthānāṃ vikalpaḥ syāt / Jaim_12,3.24 /
children.translated_text: Since <s>mantras</s> are concurrent, those serving the same purpose should be treated as <s>vikalpa</s> (alternatives). (Jaim. 12.3.24)
When prescribed with a [specific] number, there is <s>samuccaya</s> (combination), since they are not concurrent. (Jaim. 12.3.25)

children.text: brāhmaṇavihiteṣu ca saṃkhyāvat sarveṣām upadiṣṭhatvāt / Jaim_12,3.26 /
children.translated_text: And for those enjoined in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts], like those with numbers, [there is combination] since all are instructed. (Jaim. 12.3.26)
And the observation of <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) of the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse) and <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call) is likewise. (Jaim. 12.3.27)
Or there should be <s>vikalpa</s> (option), since <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) is not [explicitly] stated in scripture. (Jaim. 12.3.28)
Because the instruction serves the purpose of a subordinate element. (Jaim. 12.3.29)

children.text: vaṣaṭkāre nānārthatvāt samuccayo hautrās tu vikalperann ekārthatvāt / Jaim_12,3.30 /
children.translated_text: In the case of the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial call), there is <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) because of the multiplicity of purposes; but the <s>hautra</s> (Hotṛ's recitations) should be treated as <s>vikalpa</s> (alternatives) because they serve the same purpose. (Jaim. 12.3.30)
Or there is <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) of the <s>hautra</s> (Hotṛ's recitations), since [the statement] re-states what is [already] being performed. (Jaim. 12.3.31)
And [scripture] shows <s>samuccaya</s> (combination). (Jaim. 12.3.32)

children.text: japāś cākarmasaṃyuktāḥ stutyāśīrabhidhānāś ca yājamāneṣu samuccayaḥ syād āśīḥpṛthaktvāt / Jaim_12,4.1 /
children.translated_text: <s>Japa</s> (silent recitations) not connected with ritual action, and those expressing praise and benedictions — in rites for the benefit of the sacrificer, there should be <s>samuccaya</s> (combination), since benedictions are distinct. (Jaim. 12.4.1)
And [scripture] shows <s>samuccaya</s> (combination). (Jaim. 12.4.2)

children.text: yājyānuvākyāsu tu vikalpaḥ syād devatopalakṣaṇārthatvāt / Jaim_12,4.3 /
children.translated_text: But in the case of <s>yājyā</s> (offering verses) and <s>anuvākyā</s> (invitatory verses), there should be <s>vikalpa</s> (option), since they serve the purpose of indicating the deity. (Jaim. 12.4.3)
And because of the observation of an indicatory sign. (Jaim. 12.4.4)

children.text: krayeṣu ti vikalpaḥ syād ekārthatvāt / Jaim_12,4.5 /
children.translated_text: In purchasing [rites], there should be <s>vikalpa</s> (option), since they serve the same purpose. (Jaim. 12.4.5)
Or there is <s>samuccaya</s> (combination), because of the co-occurrence of the applied substance with the performance. (Jaim. 12.4.6)
And [scripture] shows <s>samuccaya</s> (combination). (Jaim. 12.4.7)
And in the consecration [rite], because it is subservient to that [principal rite]. (Jaim. 12.4.8)

children.text: saṃkhyāsu tu vikalpaḥ syāc chrutipratiṣedhāt / Jaim_12,4.9 /
children.translated_text: But when numbers [are prescribed], there should be <s>vikalpa</s> (option), because of the scriptural prohibition. (Jaim. 12.4.9)

children.text: dravyavikārāt tu pūrvavad arthakarma syāt tayā vikalpena niyamapradhānatvāt / Jaim_12,4.10 /
children.translated_text: But when there is modification of the substance, as in the previous [case], the purposive act should apply — by option, since restriction is primary. (Jaim. 12.4.10)

children.text: dravyatve 'pi samuccayo dravyasya karmaniṣpatteḥ pratipaśukarmabhedād evaṃ sati yathāprakṛti / Jaim_12,4.11 /
children.translated_text: Even when [it is] a substance, there is <s>samuccaya</s> (combination), since the substance is completed by the ritual act; because of the difference of act per each animal, being so, [it is] as in the <s>prakṛti</s> (model rite). (Jaim. 12.4.11)
If [one argues] that the <s>kapāla</s> (potsherds) are likewise — (Jaim. 12.4.12)
No, because the act is subservient to another [purpose]. (Jaim. 12.4.13)
But the appropriation [of the vessel] is because it is subsidiary. (Jaim. 12.4.14)
Even when [the substance is] cooked, it should be as in the previous [case]. (Jaim. 12.4.15)

children.text: vikalpyo 'nvarthakarmaniyamapradhānatvāc chese ca karmakāryasamavāyāt tasamāt tenārthakarma syāt / Jaim_12,4.16 /
children.translated_text: There should be option, since restriction is primary in the purposive act that follows, and in the remainder, because of the co-occurrence of ritual act and effect; therefore by that the purposive act should apply. (Jaim. 12.4.16)
In the case of the <s>ukhā</s> (fire-vessel), there is <s>samuccaya</s> (combination) of the optional and the obligatory, since desire is observed in the [obligatory] injunction. (Jaim. 12.4.17)
And when [the vessel] does not exist, the ritual act should apply to unconsecrated [vessels]. (Jaim. 12.4.17*)
And because that serves the purpose of the deity. (Jaim. 12.4.18)

children.text: vikāro vā nityasyāgneḥ kāmyena taduktahetuḥ / Jaim_12,4.19 /
children.translated_text: Or [it is] a modification of the obligatory [fire] by the optional one — the reason for that has been stated. (Jaim. 12.4.19)
Because of the [scriptural] statement, the ritual act should apply to unconsecrated [vessels]. (Jaim. 12.4.20)
And even in combination, there would be a fault. (Jaim. 12.4.21)

children.text: vacanād iti ced athetarasminn utsargāparigrahaḥ karmaṇaḥ kṛtatvāt / Jaim_12,4.22 /
children.translated_text: If [one argues] 'because of the [scriptural] statement' — then in the other [case] there should be no acceptance of the general rule, since the act has been performed. (Jaim. 12.4.22)
That should be the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire), because of the connection with the oblation. (Jaim. 12.4.23)
Or another [fire], since [it is] taken up and brought; in that [fire] the consecration act [applies], since it is prescribed. (Jaim. 12.4.24)
But [the elements] would lapse because of [change of] location. (Jaim. 12.4.25)

children.text: nityādhāraṇe vikalpo na hy akasmāt pratiṣedhaḥ syāt / Jaim_12,4.26 /
children.translated_text: In obligatory maintenance [of fire], there is <s>vikalpa</s> (option), for there should not be a prohibition without cause. (Jaim. 12.4.26)
Or, because of the obligatory maintenance, the prohibition [applies] to [a fire] that has lost its splendor. (Jaim. 12.4.27)

children.text: parārthāny ekaḥ pratiyantivat satrāhīnayo yajamānagaṇe 'niyamo 'viśeṣāt / Jaim_12,4.28 /
children.translated_text: In <s>satra</s> (long group sacrifice) and <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day sacrifice), [acts] for the benefit of others are [performed by] one [person] like a representative; regarding the group of sacrificers, there is no restriction, because of non-distinction. (Jaim. 12.4.28)
Or the primary [meaning] would apply, because there is no conflict. / Jaim_12,4.29 /

children.text: satre gṛhapatir asaṃyogād dhautravad āmnāyavacanāc ca / Jaim_12,4.30 /
children.translated_text: In a <s>Satra</s> (sacrificial session), the <s>Gṛhapati</s> (householder-priest) [would officiate], because of non-conjunction — like the <s>Hautra</s> (Hotṛ's function), and because of the traditional text's statement. / Jaim_12,4.30 /
Or [it is performed] by all, because it serves that purpose. / Jaim_12,4.31 /
In case of conflict, the later [rule] prevails. / Jaim_12,4.32 /
In the <s>Hautra</s> (Hotṛ's function), because it serves another's purpose. / Jaim_12,4.33 /
The explicit statement prevails. / Jaim_12,4.34 /
Because of capacity, the office of <s>ṛtvij</s> (priest) would be open to all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes). / Jaim_12,4.35 /
Or, because of <s>smṛti</s> (tradition), it would pertain [only] to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. / Jaim_12,4.36 /
And because of the injunction regarding the <s>Phalacamasa</s> (fruit-cup), [it extends] to the others. / Jaim_12,4.37 /
In the <s>Sānnāyya</s> (cooked-milk offering) too, the prohibition is likewise, because it serves as the reason for the <s>Soma</s>-drinking. / Jaim_12,4.38 /
And in the fourfold division (<s>Caturdhākaraṇa</s>), because of the explicit specification. / Jaim_12,4.39 /
And in the <s>Anvāhārya</s> (supplementary offering), because of observation. / Jaim_12,4.40 /
